standard.title: Disposable Sanitary Napkin/Panty Liner/Maternity Pad/Period Panty — Specification (Third Revision)
standard.sector: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, sizes, construction, and testing parameters for disposable (non-reusable) sanitary napkins, panty liners, maternity pads, and period panties designed for external use.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements, sizes, construction, and testing parameters for disposable (non-reusable) sanitary napkins, panty liners, maternity pads, and period panties designed for external use.

amendments.summary: No active amendments issued since publication on this copy.

certification.description: Voluntary / Statutory. Conformance with IS 5405 ensures compliance with hygiene, biocompatibility, and absorption standards. Products conforming to this standard are certified under Scheme-I and may be marked with the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards in accordance with the BIS Act, 2016. Hallmarking is completely inapplicable to technical and medical textile products.
requirements: Every product complying with this standard may be certified under BIS Scheme-I and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) under a valid licence along with the registered licence number (CM/L).
Disposable sanitary napkins, panty liners, maternity pads, and period panties basically consist of three main layers: a) cover or top sheet; b) absorbent core; and c) barrier or bottom sheet.

The cover or top sheet coming into contact with the skin must be of good quality cotton, rayon knitted sleeve, gauze, non-woven fabric, or other porous materials. If cotton gauze is used, it must conform to IS 758.

The absorbent core forming the middle layer must consist of filler materials such as cellulose pulp, cellulose wadding, tissue, cotton, wood pulp, or super absorbent materials. It must be free from unintended lumps, oil spots, dirt, or foreign matter that can cause skin injury or discomfort.
The barrier or bottom sheet must be made of suitable leak-proof material to prevent fluid pass-through, satisfying the pressure-resistance requirements after absorption.
The pH of the aqueous extract of the product must lie within the range of 3.5 to 7.5 when evaluated in accordance with IS 1390.

The products must absorb colored distilled water (tested per Annex B at 27 ± 2 °C) and withstand a 1 kg standard weight applied for 1 minute on the wet portion without showing any bottom or side leakage. The minimum fluid absorption values are: a) Sanitary Napkin: 30 ml; b) Panty Liner: 1 ml; c) Maternity Pad: 50 ml; d) Period Panty: 30 ml.

To prevent biological contamination and infection, the total viable microbial count (bacteria and fungi) must not exceed 1 000 cfu/gm. Pathogenic Staphylococcus aureus must be completely absent when evaluated per Clause 7.3.2.1.

The products must be produced under good hygienic conditions in accordance with the Good Manufacturing Practice guidelines outlined in Annex C (including separate demarcated storage, 70% Isopropyl Alcohol hand sanitizers, proper lighting, ventilation, and pest control).

If specified by the buyer, raw materials must be tested and show reactivity as 'non-cytotoxic' under IS/ISO 10993-5, and be 'Non-irritant and Non-sensitizer' when tested per IS 17932 (Part 7) and IS 17932 (Part 6) respectively.

The amount of phthalate present in the product must be less than 0.1 percent (individually or in combination) when tested at raw material stage or in the final product as per IS 9873 (Part 6) at least once a year.

If compostability is claimed, the product must pass IS/ISO 17088. If anti-bacterial activity is claimed, the raw or finished material must demonstrate an antibacterial activity value of 2 or more when evaluated as per the absorption method of IS/ISO 20743.

Each consumer pack must be legibly and indelibly marked with: manufacturer's name, size, type, quantity, directions of use, disposability instructions, batch/lot number, date of manufacture, and compostability/biocompatibility certifications (if applicable).

Finished products must be packed in rigid or flexible packages (such as carton board, PE, PP, or polyester) that protect against contaminants during shipment and storage. The packaging must be completely free of tears or damage.
